title: 1953 AHSME Problem 32
statement: Each angle of a rectangle is trisected. The intersections of the pairs of trisectors adjacent to the same side always form:

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: a quadrilateral with no special properties

solutions.text:
For each side, the two trisectors adjacent to it meet on that side’s perpendicular bisector. Opposite such intersection points are reflections across the center of the rectangle, so the diagonals of the resulting quadrilateral bisect each other. One diagonal lies on the horizontal symmetry axis and the other on the vertical symmetry axis, so they are perpendicular.

A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other is a parallelogram; if those diagonals are perpendicular, its four sides are equal. Hence the quadrilateral is a rhombus. It need not be a square because the two diagonals need not have equal length.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Use the horizontal and vertical symmetry axes of the rectangle
The four intersection points have perpendicular diagonals that bisect each other
